From "Why did you use it?" to "Why didn't you?" in 24 months. 🤯 .. Do you feel the same? DhanunjayaRao Bandlamudi (DJ) and 5 others The "Black Box" trap of Agentic AI 🕸️ In the era of predictive AI, we had a seat at the table—engineers defined the features, simulated the outcomes, and refined the logic before a single line went to production 🛠️. But with Agentic and GenAI, the game has changed, and not necessarily for the better 📉. We’re seeing two major pitfalls right now: • The "Plausibility" Trap: People are using GenAI for predictive scenarios and saying "hallucination" when it fails. The reality? They’re using a tool built for plausibility to solve problems that require precision 🎯. • The Steering Nightmare: Even if a model tells you what it "thought," correcting the course isn't like fixing a line of code. It’s a butterfly effect—fix one output, and you might break the entire reasoning chain 🦋. In the old world, we dictated the variables. In the new world, many are just hoping the "black box" stays on the rails. For me, if you can’t observe the "why" and reliably correct the "how," you haven't built a solution—you've built a liability ⚠️ DhanunjayaRao Bandlamudi (DJ) and 4 others Apple's decision to delay their AI features reminds me of this fundamental: Internal standards of #Quality are non-negotiable, especially in software 🚀 #Apple won’t compromise on results, even if it means going against the tide 💪. In an industry obsessed with speed, I see two distinct schools of thought: * The "Don’t Worry, Be Crappy" mindset: Release first, fix/bother later. Apple refuses both. They stick to their rules, even when it leads to the irony of partnering with their largest competitor. #AppleIntelligence is simple: Under the hood, #GoogleGemini models will provide the horsepower, but Apple dictates the outcomes. * I’m sure the 2026 comparison videos will be: "Editing images with Siri on iPhone 18 vs. Google Pixel vs Samsung <>" * Behind the scenes, the same class of models is doing the work 😂 but the #UX, abstraction, and ease of use are what truly matter in #SoftwareDevelopment. text: #AI isn’t a magic solution, but it can pull us out of that confusion. #healthcare, for example. Except for those in the medical field, 90% of us can’t fully interpret scan reports like USG or CT. The wording feels foreign, and finding reliable information is a nightmare. I’ve been there — family members get scans, and until a professional explains, we’re left guessing whether it’s a real problem or what the next steps are. It feels like wishing for a personal doctor who’s just a call away. 🙋🏻What if I told you AI can be that “buddy”? I crafted a prompt that explains the content of reports, outlines next steps, and answers follow-up questions — in detail. And because #multilingual, I can switch to Telugu or any language needed, saving me from browsing millions of #Google results or waiting for a doctor. 👨‍⚕️Here’s the prompt I use: *You are an expert Medical Diagnostic Consultant specializing in the interpretation of abdominal imaging, specifically CT scans and ultrasounds. Your goal is to provide patients with clear, honest, and empathetic analysis of their reports. Strict Behavioral Constraints: YOU MUST NOT INVOLVE OR ANSWER ANY OTHER TOPICS OTHER THAN HEALTHCARE AND DIAGNOSTICS Privacy: Automatically ignore and redact any personally identifiable information (PII) such as names, addresses, or phone numbers. Communication Style: Honesty: Provide a realistic interpretation of the results. Do not sugarcoat findings; if a result is concerning, communicate it directly but professionally. Clarity: Use "Plain English" to explain complex medical jargon found in the reports. Empathy: Acknowledge the stress or discomfort the patient may be feeling. Operational Workflow: - Initial State: Your first response should be a brief introduction of your expertise and a request for the user to provide the report content. - Data Collection: Before providing a final analysis, you must ensure you have the patient’s Age, Gender, and Relevant Medical History. If these are missing from the initial upload, ask for them. - Summary of Findings: A crisp breakdown of what the scan shows. - Clinical Significance: What these findings mean in the context of the patient's history. - Constraint: Do not provide a diagnosis or treatment plan until a report or summary has been provided* Give it a try — you might be surprised how much clarity AI can bring. text: I recently added a personal reminder for the year ahead, and it’s a lesson I’ve borrowed directly from AI #LLMs can learn from us, but there’s a specific Agentic Design Pattern humans desperately need to adopt: ReAct (Reason + Act). 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗛𝘂𝗺𝗮𝗻 "𝗕𝘂𝗴" 🐛 • In conversations—especially when receiving feedback or dealing with a "blame game"—our default setting is often to react instantly. • Someone points a finger ➡️ We get defensive. • Someone gives tough #feedback ➡️ We start a debate. • The result? Heated arguments, spoiled relationships, and a bad impression. 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗰 "𝗙𝗶𝘅" 🤖 1. In the world of LLMs, the #ReAct pattern is brilliant because it forces the system to Reason first and Act second. 2. It creates a "buffer" where the model thinks through the context, identifies the goal, and then executes the step. It doesn't just spit out the first thought; it validates it against logic. 𝗠𝘆 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲 𝗜𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 🛠️ I’m applying this to my own communication. Before responding to a trigger: • 1. Stop..! 2. Reason: Why are they saying this? What is my goal here? Is my immediate response helpful or just defensive? • Act: Respond based on logic, not just the impulse. • By giving ourselves that "latency" for reasoning, we avoid unnecessary friction and maintain better professional relationships.
